events.title: Management in the Maritime Industry: From Ship Construction and Commercial Shipping to Sustainable Ship Recycling
events.speakers: Mr. P. Sri Ram Krishnan, Operations Manager and Hazmat Expert, Sea Sentinels Pte. Ltd., Singapore
events.summary: Mr. P. Sri Ram Krishnan, Operations Manager and Hazmat Expert at Sea Sentinels Pte. Ltd., Singapore, on how ships are built, operated and recycled, and where managers fit in.
events.body:
The Department of Management Studies organised a guest talk titled Management in the Maritime Industry: From Ship Construction and Commercial Shipping to Sustainable Ship Recycling on 5 November 2026 in Room 6412. The guest speaker was Mr. P. Sri Ram Krishnan, Operations Manager and Hazmat Expert at Sea Sentinels Pte. Ltd., Singapore.

Guest speakerMr. P. Sri Ram Krishnan, Operations Manager and Hazmat Expert, Sea Sentinels Pte. Ltd., Singapore
VenueRoom 6412, Department of Management Studies, Saveetha Engineering College
AudienceMBA students

About the talk

The talk gave students a practical view of how the maritime industry operates across a ship's whole life. Mr. Sri Ram Krishnan covered:

  • Ship construction
  • Commercial shipping operations
  • Hazardous material management
  • Sustainable ship recycling

A recurring theme was the place of management in a technical industry. As one of his slides put it, not everyone working in a shipyard is an engineer: engineers design and build the ship, while management professionals plan and monitor the project, manage cost and budget, arrange people and resources, coordinate with suppliers, clients and stakeholders, and make sure the ship is delivered on time.

Outcome

The session gave students an industry view of operational practice in the maritime sector, along with the career opportunities it offers management graduates and the growing importance of sustainability in shipping.

events.title: Business Development and the Art of Building Relationships
events.speakers: Ms. Priya Dey, Global Business Development Consultant
events.summary: Global Business Development Consultant Ms. Priya Dey on business development, leadership, customer experience and the art of building professional relationships.
events.body:
The Department of Management Studies organised an alumni referral industry expert talk titled Business Development and the Art of Building Relationships on Friday, 25 September 2026, from 1.00 pm to 3.00 pm in Room 6411, Saveetha Engineering College. Aligned with SDG 4 - Quality Education, the session brought together the resource person, faculty members and MBA students.

Resource personMs. Priya Dey, Global Business Development Consultant
Areas of focusHospitality, business development, leadership and customer experience
VenueRoom 6411, Saveetha Engineering College
ParticipantsMBA students and faculty

Objective

The talk set out to familiarise MBA students with the fundamentals and practical side of business development and relationship building: how business opportunities are developed, how professional networks are built and how customer relationships are strengthened, connecting management concepts with real-world practice.

About the session

Ms. Dey spoke on why developing and sustaining meaningful professional relationships matters in business, and on the links between business development, relationship building and customer experience. She also drew out the role of leadership and relationship management across business settings, including the hospitality sector, and encouraged students to treat relationship-building as a core managerial competency.

Highlights

  • Business development and its role in organisational growth
  • The art of building and maintaining professional relationships
  • Relationship management in hospitality and customer-facing businesses
  • Leadership in developing productive business connections
  • Customer experience as part of business development

Outcome

Students gained a clearer sense of why business development matters in a competitive environment, the value of professional networking and relationship-building skills, and how leadership, customer experience and business relationships connect, relating management concepts to practical business and hospitality settings. The programme also strengthened industry-academia interaction.

The talk mapped to Programme Outcomes PO1 (business problem solving and decision making), PO2 (leadership and team management), PO4 (professional communication and collaboration) and PO6 (global outlook, entrepreneurial thinking and lifelong learning).

events.title: Awareness is the First Line of Defence against Fraud
events.speakers: Mrs. Sudha Hari Priya, Deputy Vice President, and Mr. Karthikeyan S (alumnus, 2022 batch), Credit Intelligence and Control Manager, HDFC Bank Ltd.
events.summary: An alumni-led cyber fraud awareness session by Mrs. Sudha Hari Priya, Deputy Vice President, and alumnus Mr. Karthikeyan S (2022 batch), Credit Intelligence and Control Manager, HDFC Bank Ltd.
events.body:
The Department of Management Studies organised an alumni-led awareness session titled Awareness is the First Line of Defence against Fraud on Wednesday, 12 August 2026, from 11.00 am to 12.00 noon at Lines Hall, Saveetha Engineering College. Two resource persons from HDFC Bank Ltd., one of them an alumnus of the department, spoke to MBA students on cyber fraud and safe digital behaviour. It followed the alumni talk The Road to Corporate Success by Mr. Karthikeyan S earlier that morning.

Resource personsMrs. Sudha Hari Priya, Deputy Vice President (Process Head - Credit Intelligence and Control), HDFC Bank Ltd.
Mr. Karthikeyan S, alumnus (MBA 2022 batch), Credit Intelligence and Control Manager, HDFC Bank Ltd.
VenueLines Hall, Saveetha Engineering College
ParticipantsMBA students and faculty
Alumni coordinatorsDr. R. Divya Ranjani and Dr. S. Poorani, Assistant Professors

Objective

The session set out to make students aware of cyber fraud and the importance of safe digital behaviour: to help them recognise online threats, take care on digital platforms, and see awareness as the first line of defence against fraud.

About the session

Drawing on their work in credit intelligence and control at HDFC Bank, the resource persons explained why vigilance matters in everyday digital activity and walked students through fraud risks using the bank's awareness campaign material. The campaign visuals focused on two common traps: careless screen sharing and downloading fake APK apps.

Highlights

  • What cyber fraud looks like and why caution matters when using digital services
  • Warning signs of suspicious or fraudulent activity
  • Being careful with screen sharing and protecting personal information
  • Avoiding fake or unverified APK apps
  • Building responsible digital habits and passing cyber-safety awareness on to others

Outcome

Students came away with an industry view of cyber fraud and a clearer sense of how to stay alert to fraud attempts, protect sensitive information, avoid suspicious links and apps, and encourage safe online practice among their peers. The session also strengthened alumni-student engagement in the department.

The session aligned with SDG 4 - Quality Education and SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, and mapped to Programme Outcomes PO1 (business problem solving and decision making), PO4 (professional communication and collaboration) and PO6 (global outlook, entrepreneurial thinking and lifelong learning).

events.speakers: Mr. Karthikeyan S (alumnus, 2022 batch), Credit Intelligence and Control Manager, HDFC Bank Ltd.
events.summary: Alumnus Mr. Karthikeyan S (MBA 2022 batch), Credit Intelligence and Control Manager at HDFC Bank Ltd., on his career in banking and staying safe from cyber fraud.
events.body:
The Department of Management Studies organised an alumni talk titled The Road to Corporate Success: An Alumnus Journey in Banking on Wednesday, 12 August 2026, from 10.00 am to 11.00 am at Lines Hall, Saveetha Engineering College. Mr. Karthikeyan S, an alumnus of the department's MBA 2022 batch, spoke to MBA students about his career in banking, with a focus on cyber fraud awareness. Aligned with SDG 4 - Quality Education, the talk was followed by the session Awareness is the First Line of Defence against Fraud with Mrs. Sudha Hari Priya of HDFC Bank.

Resource personMr. Karthikeyan S, alumnus (MBA 2022 batch), Credit Intelligence and Control Manager, HDFC Bank Ltd.
VenueLines Hall, Saveetha Engineering College
ParticipantsMBA students
Alumni coordinatorsDr. R. Divya Ranjani and Dr. S. Poorani, Assistant Professors

Objective

The talk set out to give students a practical view of the banking sector and the careers it offers in financial services, and to build awareness of cyber fraud, digital banking risks and safe financial practice, bridging classroom learning and working life through the experience of a recent alumnus.

About the session

Mr. Karthikeyan traced his journey from the MBA programme into banking and his current role in credit intelligence and control at HDFC Bank. Cyber fraud awareness was the centre of the talk: he explained why customers need to stay alert when using digital financial services and online transactions, and how banking professionals protect customers, spot suspicious activity and keep trust in the financial system.

Highlights

  • An alumnus's career path and growth in the banking sector
  • Cyber fraud and the common risks in digital finance
  • Taking care with digital banking and online transactions
  • The work of credit intelligence, control and risk monitoring teams
  • Professional responsibility, continuous learning and staying current with the industry

Outcome

Students came away with a clearer picture of career paths and roles in banking, the importance of cyber safety and responsible digital financial practice, and how credit intelligence and control fit into banking operations. Hearing an alumnus's own journey helped them connect management and finance concepts to real industry functions, and the talk strengthened alumni-student engagement in the department.

events.title: Industrial Visit: Diamond Group
events.summary: Heavy steel fabrication, welding, machining and shop-floor safety at Diamond Group ("Anything in Steel"), Chennai.
events.body:
On 18 March 2026, students and faculty members of the Department of Management Studies visited the manufacturing facility of Diamond Group, a Chennai steel fabrication company whose motto is "Anything in Steel". The visit gave students a close look at heavy steel fabrication, welding, material handling and machining, and at how a large engineering shop floor is planned and run.

Objectives

  • Observe how steel structures and components are fabricated, welded and machined on an industrial scale
  • Understand material handling, shop-floor layout and workplace safety in a heavy engineering unit
  • Relate operations management and production planning to real practice
  • Interact with engineers and technicians and learn about careers in the fabrication industry

About the organisation

Diamond Group operates through Diamond Engineering (Chennai) Private Limited (DECPL), which was taken over in 1987 and grew into a fabricator of heavy steel structures and equipment for customers in India and abroad.

Safety briefing

Before entering the shop floor, students were briefed on safety rules: protective equipment, marked walkways, and keeping clear of moving loads and welding areas. Workers on the floor wore protective overalls, and visitors stayed with their guides throughout.

Fabrication and welding shop

The fabrication bay is a large hall served by overhead cranes. Heavy steel sections move along roller conveyors to the welding station, where welders join the parts while a large fixture holds them in position. Students watched the welding from a safe distance and saw how handling, alignment and welding are arranged as one flow to keep heavy work accurate and safe.

Machine shop

In the machine shop, students saw lathes, milling and shaping machines, with machined components stacked beside them. A shop-floor technician explained how each machine is set up and how components are finished to the required size, and faculty members joined the students in asking questions about the process.

Interaction with industry staff

In the interaction session, students asked about fabrication methods, quality checks, safety practices and the skills the industry looks for in young professionals.

Key takeaways

  • Heavy fabrication relies on careful planning of material flow, handling equipment and workstations
  • Welding and machining quality depends on skilled operators, correct set-up and regular inspection
  • Safety rules are an essential part of everyday work on a heavy engineering shop floor
  • Seeing real equipment in operation makes operations concepts far clearer than textbooks alone

The department thanks the management, engineers and technicians of Diamond Group for hosting the visit and guiding the students.

events.body:
The Department of Management Studies organised an alumni talk titled Campus to Career: Crafting Your Pathway to Success on Saturday, 7 February 2026, from 1.00 pm to 3.00 pm at Lattice Hall, Saveetha Engineering College. Aligned with SDG 4 - Quality Education, the session drew 230 MBA students.

Resource personMs. V. Keerthana, alumna (batch 2022-2024), Associate (Reconciliation), State Street
VenueLattice Hall, Saveetha Engineering College
Participants230 MBA students
Alumni coordinatorsDr. R. Divya Ranjani and Dr. S. Poorani, Assistant Professors

Objective

The talk set out to build students' career preparedness, employability skills and industry awareness, and to bridge the gap between academic learning and professional expectations through the practical experience of a recent alumna.

About the session

Ms. Keerthana guided students through the transition from campus to corporate life, stressing that professional competencies must grow alongside academic knowledge. She covered career planning, adaptability and organisational expectations, and shared her own career journey: the challenges of her early working years and the strategies she used to overcome them.

Highlights

  • Moving from academic life to corporate culture
  • Employability skills: communication, teamwork and analytical thinking
  • Industry expectations and professional ethics
  • Handling early-career challenges and building skills continuously
  • Lifelong learning as a driver of career growth

The session was interactive, with students joining the discussion and clearing their career-related queries.

Programme

Welcome addressMs. Hellen, MBA student
Guest introductionMs. Sowmiya, MBA student
Felicitation of the alumnaDr. G. Ramasundaram, Dean; Dr. Joseph Sathish; Dr. A. Vanitha; Dr. K. Selvi
Alumni talkMs. V. Keerthana, alumna (2022-2024)
Vote of thanksMs. Sarena Edward, MBA student

Outcome

Students came away with a clearer picture of corporate work culture and industry expectations, the skills needed for career success, and the opportunities and growth paths open to them, and said they felt more confident and motivated to prepare for professional roles. In the feedback survey, respondents rated the event 4.59 out of 5, with 62.5% giving it the top rating.

The talk mapped to Programme Outcomes PO1 (business problem solving and decision making), PO2 (leadership and team management), PO4 (professional communication and collaboration) and PO6 (global outlook, entrepreneurial thinking and lifelong learning).

  • Adaptability in new situations

events.title: Industrial Visit: NLC India Limited, Mine-IA, Neyveli
events.summary: Open-cast lignite mining, safety discipline and large-scale operations management at NLC India's Mine-IA, Neyveli.
events.body:
As part of the MBA curriculum, the Department of Management Studies organised an industrial visit to the Mine-IA unit of NLC India Limited (formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation), Neyveli, on 20 January 2023. Students and faculty members took part in the visit, which gave first-hand exposure to large-scale mining operations, plant management and public sector organisational culture.

Objectives

  • Understand the working of a large public sector enterprise in the energy and mining sector
  • Observe how operations, logistics, safety and human resources are managed on a large scale
  • Relate operations management, supply chain, HRM and CSR concepts to real practice
  • Interact with industry professionals and gain career awareness

About the organisation

NLC India Limited is a Government of India enterprise under the Ministry of Coal and one of the country's leading lignite mining and power generation companies. Headquartered in Chennai, with its principal operations at Neyveli in Cuddalore district, it mines lignite and uses it to generate electricity in its thermal power stations. Its Neyveli mines (Mine-I, Mine-IA and Mine-II) are among the best-known open-cast lignite mines in India, and the company has also expanded into renewable energy.

Orientation and safety briefing

The visit began with an introduction by the Public Relations department, covering the company's history, its role in the nation's energy supply and its operating units. Students were briefed on personal protective practices, restricted zones and conduct inside the mine area.

Mine operations

Students observed the open-cast mining process, in which overburden is removed to expose the lignite seam, and the lignite is then excavated and moved by large machinery and conveyor systems to the consuming plants. The coordination between mining, transport and power generation showed how complex operations planning and logistics are in a continuous-process industry.

Management insights

  • Operations management: continuous production, capacity utilisation, equipment maintenance and scheduling
  • Supply chain: movement of lignite from the mine to the power stations with minimal storage and delay
  • Human resource management: shift-based work, skill-based roles, training and employee welfare in a large public sector workforce
  • Health, safety and environment: safety protocols, dust and water management, land reclamation and plantation around the mine area
  • Corporate social responsibility: community development activities for people in the surrounding region

Interaction with officials

Officials answered students' questions about operations, career paths, recruitment in public sector undertakings and the future of the energy sector, including the shift towards renewable energy.

Key takeaways

  • Large industrial operations depend on precise planning, coordination and discipline
  • Safety and environmental responsibility are integral to business success
  • Public sector enterprises play a vital role in national development and employment
  • Practical exposure helps students connect management theory with real decisions
